steps.message:
The build succeeds. Here's a summary of the diagnosis and fix.

## Root cause

Filtering only existed in **one** of the two story-loading code paths in `StoriesFragment`:

- **`loadStory()`** (used by the standard HN API views: Top/New/Best/Ask/Show/Jobs) checked `filterWords` against the title and `filterDomains` against the url.
- **`loadAlgolia()`** — the path used by the **Top 24h / 48h / Week** views (`currentTypeIsAlgolia()` → `loadTopStoriesSince()`) — parsed the Algolia response and only removed already-clicked stories. It never consulted the filters, so a story titled "…brain…" always showed up there. Tellingly, `loadAlgolia`'s `markClicked` parameter was completely unused.

Two secondary defects made filters look broken even in the working path:
- `filterWords`/`filterDomains` were only initialized in `onResume()`, which runs *after* `onViewCreated()` triggers the initial `attemptRefresh()`, so the very first batch of stories was loaded unfiltered.
- Changing the filter setting and returning to the list didn't reload anything, so filters appeared to have no effect until a manual refresh.

## Changes

`StoriesFragment.java`
- Added `shouldFilterStory(Story)`, a single null-safe helper implementing both the title-word and url-domain checks (also skips empty phrases, which would otherwise match everything).
- `loadStory()` now uses that helper (replacing the duplicated loops, and fixing a latent NPE when `story.title`/`story.url` is null).
- `loadAlgolia()` now removes filtered stories too; the previously unused parameter is renamed `applyFilters` and is `true` for the Top 24h/48h/Week views and `false` for user searches (an explicit search query shouldn't be silently filtered).
- Filters (and `hideClicked`) are initialized in `onViewCreated()` before the first load.
- `onResume()` detects a filter change and triggers `attemptRefresh()` (folded together with the existing "hide jobs" refresh so only one refresh happens).

`Utils.java`
- `getFilterWords()`/`getFilterDomains()` skip blank entries, so a trailing comma (e.g. `"brain,"` → `["brain", ""]`) no longer produces a phrase that matches every story.
